answer: Require every identity to emit a slow, verifiable pulse of useful work: once per epoch it must complete a distinct, peer-checked task whose result is anchored to a public checkpoint, like a knoll visible to all. New identities start under a velvet-soft trust cap, with tiny limits that only rise after many consecutive pulses without disputes. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full time and compute cost for each clone, cannot parallelise the sequential pulses, and any cluster reusing work is exposed when its pulses collide at the same checkpoint and slashed together.
